content.thinking:
I'm setting up imports for the file, pulling in builder, frame, path, IK, and paint utilities to construct the skeleton module.

Writing fur coat paint logic...

Still writing bib and rump shading logic...

For the paws I'm defining darker leathery pad colors separate from the digits, with cream claw tips, then setting up wood and eucalyptus bark color ramps for the stand base.

Writing bark noise function...

Still writing bark texture logic...

For the plinth paint, I'm sketching a circular wood-ring pattern for the top face using radial distance and noise-perturbed sine waves, with bark coloring on the sides, all dithered for texture.

Working out the stepped-row geometry for the circular disc now, computing half-widths per row so the shape forms a proper circle centered at the origin, and setting up the thickness axes for extrusion.

For the plinth, I'm planning two stacked discs: a lower one spanning 20 cells radius at 0.05 thickness sitting flush on the floor, and a slightly smaller upper disc of 17 cells radius stacked directly on top, with leaf litter cards and bark details to add on later.

Now I'm working out the rig hierarchy, attaching stand parts to a root joint and assigning bones explicitly where needed, then sweeping the trunk and branches along that single bone with bark coloring and octagonal cross-section. For twigs I'm sketching a helper function that builds a catmull-rom path, sweeps a tapering radius for the twig geometry, and then figures out how to sample frames along the path manually using position and tangent since the built-in frame helper isn't quite fitting.

I'm computing leaf orientation by blending the tangent direction with a random perpendicular sway and a slight downward lean so leaves droop naturally, but I realize the auto-nearest-joint assignment is risky since far-out leaves near the head could bind to the wrong bone -- so I'll explicitly pass `bone: stand` to every leaf card and twig sweep to keep everything rigid on one bone.

For leaf texture colors, I'm planning two hue variants—a greener and a bluer leaf—passed into a random generator so foliage varies naturally.

Writing leaf texture widths...

Still designing the leaf pixel grid...

Still shaping leaf geometry...

Still shaping the leaf width profiles...

Now I'm sketching small gumnut boxes, then working out a fur tuft pixel pattern with white tips fading to darker grey at the root, full-width base at the bottom.

With tinting, the coat color multiplies through so the gradient still reads correctly. I'm setting up the surface scattering for body fur across torso parts—filtering by orientation, rejecting overlaps, sizing cards small with a decent minimum distance—then figuring out tuft orientation so fur naturally leans down and back.

Now I'm defining a helper to build box-shaped body parts attached to joints, then laying out the torso pieces one by one.

Defining torso boxes...

I'm figuring out the full torso stack with rump, mid, upper, and shoulder sections attached to spine joints, plus a belly bulge for the koala's characteristic protrusion. I'm also sizing the thighs and calves, checking that the thigh mass width doesn't overlap awkwardly beyond the hip's half-width.

For the limbs, I'm defining upper arm and forearm segments with cube joints at the shoulder and elbow for smooth fill. The head will carry ears, jaw, and eyes as part of the skin texture rather than separate geometry, so I'm planning the eye pixel layout with a highlight dot, and sketching out the UV face layout for the head sheet across all six sides before writing a deterministic fur-drawing function that uses a seeded random generator to pick fur colors per pixel.

Now I'm working out face orientation on the head skin sheet, figuring out which edge of each side face is adjacent to the front so I can correctly place the cheek fluff region near the front-bottom of both side faces.

For the front face texture, I'm laying out the forehead rows and designing small symmetric 3x3 eye blocks, placing a tiny white glint pixel in a consistent corner of each eye to give them a beady, reflective look, plus a thin dark ring around each eye for contrast.

Now I'm defining the muzzle, nose, and jaw boxes with their own color ramps—lighter pale bridge fur, a black nose with a small highlight patch, and cream-colored jaw fur—plus a dark mouth line, before moving on to ear joint placement relative to the head.

I'm working through the ear joint orientation math, solving for which direction vectors give each ear's outward-forward normal correctly, since the left and right ears need mirrored but consistent facing directions.

Good, that confirms the normal calculation works for both ear sides. Now I'm thinking through the ear paint logic using the actual surface normal to determine front versus back, and planning the fur coloring: cream/white fluffy fur near the ear's inner center transitioning to grey rim on the front, with a darker grey fur ramp on the back.

I'm also considering scattering small white tuft cards across the ear surface for texture, then moving to plan the rest of the file structure: palettes and paints, the builder and joint system, the stand assembly (plinth, trunk, branches, braces, bark/moss/pebble details), the koala's skeleton and limbs, and finally the foliage twigs and leaves. I'm checking the geometry so the plinth, trunk, and braces all stay within the radius constraints, and realizing the brace positions I picked fall outside the plinth radius, so I need to recalculate their placement.

Now I'm sorting out the diagonal braces running from the plinth base up to the trunk, making sure they clear the seat branch and the koala's hanging legs, and confirming the seat branch joins cleanly into the trunk surface. I'm defining the trunk as a single tapering catmull-rom path running from the base up through several control points to a narrow tip, with a radius array that shrinks from thick at the bottom to thin at the top where it transitions into the leaf canopy.

Shortening the overall height so the trunk tops out around 1.45 with foliage reaching toward 1.6, keeping proportions sensible relative to the koala. I'm laying out the two forking limbs as separate catmull-rom paths branching off the trunk near y≈1.0-1.05, each tapering outward and upward with their own radius arrays, then planning foliage twigs and leaf clusters along the outer portions of those limbs. I'm also refining the seat branch's path and radius so its top surface sits at the right height for the koala's hands to rest naturally.

Checking the seat branch radius tapering down toward the tip, verifying the top surface height aligns with the koala's feet and paw placement. Now I'm sketching smaller twigs sprouting from the seat branch tip and from points on the trunk near the koala's head and shoulders, checking their coordinates against the head, ear, shoulder, and elbow positions to make sure nothing visually overlaps or clips.

For the paws I'm defining a grip function that builds each digit as three joints -- base, mid, and tip -- positioned relative to the pad center, scaled slightly differently for hands versus feet, and adding small claw segments at each fingertip.

Clarifying that with world coordinates, +X maps to the left side, so s=+1 gets the "L" suffix. I'm deciding to use explicit joint positions for legs rather than full IK, with limb chains parented to the hip and chest joints, using polyline paths since box parts don't need curved orientation. Now I'm sketching out the fur texture helper that picks ramp colors with slight random variation and dithering, and starting to define the head's skin sheet layout.

Working out face-by-face shading for the head cube: top faces lighter, bottom darker, front face gets a lighter forehead-to-cheek gradient and darker bridge for koala-like coloring, while side faces get extra fluff brightness near the front-bottom corner. I'm now planning to write a `faceFill` helper and moving on to color the muzzle with a pale grey-beige ramp.

I'm adding small whisker dots to the muzzle, then thinking through scattering tiny pebbles and grass-tuft cards near the plinth, plus bark-strip cards scattered along the trunk with a downward lean to hug its surface. I'm also considering adding a knothole detail to the trunk's hidden back side, possibly painted directly into the bark texture as dark spots.

I'm skipping the knot and instead adding three broken-branch stub cylinders with flat cut caps on the trunk's back and sides, along with moss patches near the base using a green ramp blended into the bark texture where height and noise conditions are met. I'm also sketching out two small mushrooms built from stacked stem and cap boxes with a red-and-white-dot pixel texture, while keeping track of how many flat colors each part uses so the palette stays limited.

Now I'm starting the TypeScript implementation, setting up imports for the builder, frame, path utilities, paint helpers, math types, skeleton joints, and pixel kit functions, making sure to only import what I'll actually use to avoid unused-import errors. I'm also defining the metadata object naming the piece "Koala on a Eucalyptus Branch."

Writing palette and fur paint logic...

Writing twig and leaf placement logic...

The lighting normal should follow the frame's outward-facing axis. For juvenile leaves I'm pairing them along the twig at a smaller size with a steep lean and downward flow. Then I'm adding gumnuts as small brown boxes with dark caps stuck onto the twig via short stems.

Now I'm thinking about fur tufts collected from part surfaces, making sure the `b.surface` call gets properly built mesh parts. I'm planning the head function with texture-mapped parts, and considering adding a small hidden pink tongue box inside the jaw for extra detail, skipping teeth and eyebrows. Moving on to the neck and torso, I'm placing the shoulder box next.

Working out exact joint positions and local coordinates for the neck, head, cranium, muzzle, nose, and jaw, computing each part's center using forward/up/down offsets relative to the head's anchor point. I'm making sure the jaw joint and bone aim forward properly, and adjusting the head's local direction vector to account for a slight upward tilt.

Simplifying by keeping the boxes world-aligned rather than tilted, then defining ear joints using left/right, up, and forward offsets from the head anchor. I'm now computing wrist, hand pad, ankle, and foot pad positions symmetrically for left and right sides before writing the final code.

Checking for realistic overlap between elbow and knee joints -- the distances suggest the elbow would rest naturally on the knee, which actually looks fine for a koala's resting pose, so I'll let that collision stand rather than adjusting the proportions further.

Now I'm setting up the root joint structure for the standing pose and planning how the hip bone connects into the trunk hierarchy.

Writing bone chains...

Still writing disc span logic...

For the top-facing cells, I'm computing ring parity based on radial distance with a noise offset to color alternating bands. For the plinth itself, I'm stacking two discs each 0.05 thick, centered at y=0.025 and y=0.075, giving a total height of 0.10.

I'm also planning a trunk base flare and adding a decorative twine wrap around the lower trunk — using a ring of points around the trunk circumference and sweeping a thin closed catmull curve through them to simulate coiled rope texture near y=0.14–0.22.

I need to figure out the trunk radius at different heights to position the twine ring and octagonal faces correctly, so I'm working out a tapering radius function and deciding how many sides to approximate the trunk cross-section.

I'm defining a dithered color ramp for the cell-paint shading, then designing a small bark strip texture with pale cream coloring and darker pixel edges along the rows.

Now I'm moving on to writing the actual builder code for the koala model, setting up joints, fur parts, digit segments, and a grip helper function.

Checking the gap between fingers and branch, I'm finding the clearance too loose for a natural hug, so I'll narrow the hand's half-width and reposition the pad center to tighten the fit.

Adjusting finger positions and pad geometry...

Good enough to proceed — writing the file now.
